newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed after gold selloff.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed after gold selloff.

text.p: NY precious metals ended mixed, with a quick selloff in gold pulling the rest of the complex down, apart from platinum which remained firmer.
A bullion dealer said the late selloff was due to booksquaring by day traders.
COMEX December gold settled 20 cents lower at $386.10 an ounce, traded $387.00 to $386.00. The market soon bounced back from resistance at $387.00 traders said earlier.
John Brimelow, director of international equities at BV Capital Markets, said the selloff just before close was partly linked to huge short positions held by speculators.

"I imagine anyone with that sort of position would be reluctant to see the gold price rallying," Brimelow said. "It looks like some shorts were put on with a view there would be IMF gold sales, but they are not looking all that likely and physical demand is still there. That's a dangerous position to be in and they have this serious job of retreat to conduct."

COMEX volume was low at 14,000 lots as the market trod water. The IMF on Friday delayed a decision on whether to sell some five million ounces of its reserves. A board meeting is due to discuss the issue further on Wednesday.
"If it's five million ounces, it's probably priced in the market," the bullion dealer said.
Bullion was last quoted at $382.70/$383.20 an ounce.
COMEX December silver went out 0.70 cent firmer at $5.078 an ounce, traded $5.125 to $5.065.
NYMEX October platinum settled firmer, up $1.20 at $390.90 an ounce as members of the industry gathered in New York for Thursday's NYMEX platinum dinner.
There was conflicting talk of faltering platinum demand in Japan.
NYMEX December palladium went out 40 cents weaker at $122.50 an ounce.
